main_text.p: dem adveniunt, horum animalium plumis, pilis, pelIibufque infidentibus & inhærent. Sed neque hoc probat attractionem in distans; Si enim quid attrahunt ejusmodi animalia vi sui caloris, ob spiritus exhalantes, non nisi id attrahunt, quod corporibus ipsorum vicinum exiftit: sed nec occiduntur ejusmodi animalia quòd sint calidiora præ aliis, ficque vi caloris plus aliis attrahunt; nam & vi caloris, atque evaporationis vehementioris, plus aliis repellunt à suis corporibus; velut lupe-rius (ubi Secundum Princip. declarabatur,) dicebantur juvenes (ipsissima verba Illustrissimi viri refero,) ob sanguinis ebullitionem, & temperamentum calidum, magnam spirituum copiam e corpore propellere, qui cum eorum (va-porum,) quos lux crepera excutit, vires longè superent, illos repellunt, impediuntque, ut non tanta efficacia in corpora, ex quibus spiritus isti profluunt agere possint, quàm solent in illos.

page.notes: Page number 415 printed as "41§" (ornamented 5), read as 415. Several words in the running text are blurred; "pelIibufque" and "illustrissimi" readings are uncertain. The text is run together where the scan is unclear; the transcription of the final sentence is partly reconstructed and may contain errors.
